Modified read using Beige Book insights:
- Activity and labor: The Fed notes activity picking up and a tight labor market; the Beige Book corroborates strong employment across districts with continued job gains. Firms are offering more job flexibility to attract/retain workers, and districts report ongoing wage growth and wage rate increases.
- Prices and costs: Inflation pressures are broad-based. The Beige Book highlights higher energy costs being passed through via fuel surcharges and widespread wage-driven cost pressures, reinforcing elevated inflation.
- Supply chains and global headwinds: COVID-related lockdowns in China are exacerbating supply disruptions, and consumer activity has been impacted by COVID waves; the Russia-Ukraine war adds to price pressures.
- Policy stance: Decisively hawkish—75 bp hike, higher administered rates, and ongoing balance-sheet runoff.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS cross-check): Domestic banks on net eased standards for C&I and multifamily and eased on credit cards; demand strengthened for HELOCs and autos, while residential real estate demand softened. Foreign banks tightened C&I, a cross-border headwind.

Net: The Beige Book amplifies the breadth and persistence of cost and wage pressures and shows pass-through to prices, while domestic credit supply remains accommodative for many businesses and some consumers, cushioning near-term growth. Housing shows early cooling, and foreign-bank tightening is a drag. Overall tone edges slightly more negative than before.
